assets.note: Free front-end library for this dashboard use.

assets.name: @okta/okta-react 6.9.0
assets.note: Login library matching the described Okta SSO.

assets.note: Free chart library for dashboard graphs.

assets.name: highcharts 11.4.0
assets.note: Paid chart library that needs a bought licence.

audience.detail: README says internal dashboard for the support team with company SSO (Okta) on the office cluster.

assessment.data_detail: Shows open support tickets and on-call info plus staff SSO login, so it handles customer and staff personal data.

deployment.detail: Dockerfile, Kubernetes file, and CI file exist but all look like empty stubs with no image, ingress, secrets, or build jobs.

assessment.headline: Internal support dashboard with real SSO and deploy stubs, blocked by a paid chart licence and unfinished launch setup.

issues.ai_prompt: In package.json and src/App.jsx, remove the 'highcharts' dependency and all 'import Highcharts' usage and rewrite those charts using only chart.js 4.4.3. Show me the diff and confirm no highcharts import remains.
issues.explain: Highcharts is a paid product, not free like React or Chart.js. No licence proof or CREDITS file was found, so use could trigger a bill or takedown.
issues.recommendation: Buy a Highcharts licence or replace it with Chart.js which is already included.
issues.title: Paid Highcharts used with no licence proof

issues.ai_prompt: Fill in deploy/k8s-deployment.yaml for ops-dashboard with image, 2 replicas, containerPort, envFrom secret okta-credentials, ClusterIP service, and an internal-only Ingress with TLS. Do not paste secret values, only secret references.
issues.explain: The Kubernetes file only sets replicas with no image, port, secrets, or network rules. It cannot safely run as-is.
issues.recommendation: Complete the deployment with image, resource limits, Okta secrets via Kubernetes Secrets, and internal-only ingress with HTTPS.
issues.title: Kubernetes file is incomplete stub

issues.ai_prompt: Rewrite Dockerfile to use node:20-alpine as build, copy package files first, run npm ci and build, then use a non-root nginx or serve runtime, expose port, add USER node, HEALTHCHECK, and no secrets in the image.
issues.evidence: Dockerfile: COPY . /app + RUN cd /app && npm ci && npm run build + CMD ["npx","serve","/app/dist"]
issues.explain: Dockerfile copies everything, runs as root, and serves without HTTPS or health checks. Okta keys could leak if baked in.
issues.recommendation: Use multi-stage build, non-root user, .dockerignore, and pass Okta settings at run time, not in the image.
issues.title: Dockerfile not production ready

issues.ai_prompt: In src/App.jsx show the full Okta Security config with issuer, clientId from env vars, redirect URI, and LoginCallback route, and ensure all routes require login with no public access.
issues.explain: SSO wrapper is there but the auth config and login checks are not shown. If misconfigured the internal ticket data could be open to the internet.
issues.recommendation: Verify Okta issuer and client ID come from secrets, force login on all pages, and restrict network to VPN/intranet.
issues.title: SSO protection not proven complete

issues.ai_prompt: In .github/workflows/ci.yml replace the single 'on: push' line with a full workflow that on push installs, lints, builds, builds the Docker image, and deploys to the office cluster only on main.
issues.explain: CI file is only one line with no jobs to test, build, or check licences. Broken code could ship unchecked.
issues.recommendation: Add full CI jobs for install, build, Docker build, and gated deploy to the office cluster.
issues.title: CI pipeline is empty stub

issues.ai_prompt: Create LICENSE file text for proprietary internal use matching package.json UNLICENSED private true, or if open-sourcing replace with MIT text. Keep package.json and LICENSE in sync.
issues.evidence: LICENSE (0 KB empty) + package.json: private true, license UNLICENSED
issues.explain: LICENSE file is empty while package.json claims UNLICENSED private. Staff and reviewers cannot tell reuse rules.
issues.recommendation: Add one-line proprietary notice to LICENSE or add a full licence text and keep it matching package.json.
issues.title: LICENSE file empty and unclear

issues.ai_prompt: Add an internal PRIVACY.md explaining what ticket and on-call personal data the ops dashboard shows, who can access it, retention, and Okta logging contact, and link it in README.md.
issues.explain: Dashboard shows support tickets which usually contain customer names and contact details, plus staff SSO data, with no handling notice.
issues.recommendation: Add internal privacy notice and access rules for ticket data, even if no public policy is needed.
issues.title: No privacy notice for ticket data

license.detail: package.json says UNLICENSED private true but the LICENSE file is empty, so reuse rules are unclear.

mobile.detail: No mobile or desktop signals; code is a React web dashboard served as static files.

strengths: Clearly scoped as internal staff-only with Okta SSO described in code and README.
No risky images, fonts, or copy-pasted media found.
Docker plus Kubernetes plus CI intent matches the office-cluster plan.
assessment.summary: Ops Dashboard is an internal React web app for support staff to view tickets and on-call status via Okta login, hosted on the office Kubernetes cluster. It has the right private scope and basic Docker and cluster files, but they are stubs. It cannot ship until the paid Highcharts licence is sorted and deployment, SSO config, and data handling are finished.
